versions.changelog: A login refused with NoPermission gets an authored error naming the target and doctor, not the raw fault
Roles for network callers (HLD §18): declares role metadata so vmware-policy 1.24.0 can limit each token to a role's tools and targets.
Security fix: tools may not read or write the server's own control files; over HTTPS host files only inside VMWARE_MCP_FILE_ROOT. Needs vmware-policy 1.23.1.
NotAuthenticated now names both causes (expired session or missing vSphere role); needs vmware-policy 1.23.0.
Session pools: calls on one target run side by side over HTTPS (HLD §16 D-13(2)); needs vmware-policy 1.22.0. get_access_info self-diagnosis.
mcp --transport https: serve MCP over HTTPS with bearer tokens (HLD §16)
mcp --expose read / --allow-write: offer only read tools plus chosen write tools
Supervisor /wcp/login goes to the Supervisor endpoint (VKS#13); optional supervisor_host
kubeconfig tools renamed issue_supervisor_kubeconfig / issue_tkc_kubeconfig (they issue a credential); requires vmware-policy>=1.19.0
2.0: MCP tools renamed verb-first (see RELEASE_NOTES for the old -> new table); requires vmware-policy >= 1.18
MCP instructions now name the configured targets and how to choose one; a config that cannot be read says so instead of falling silent.
Destructive MCP tools preview by default (confirm=False) and state their blast radius; confirm=True refuses on blockers or unreadable measurements. Requires vmware-policy>=1.17.0.
A stopped MCP server exits within five seconds even if its logout hangs
Stopping the MCP server now logs out its vCenter session.
CLI reads are audited under their MCP tool names; every CLI command declares what it reaches (needs vmware-policy 1.15.0)

A kubeconfig is credential access on every surface: the kubeconfig tools are no longer annotated read-only and carry a medium risk level, and -o writes the file atomically and owner-only. CLI writes are authorised and audited under their MCP tool names.
a dropped connection no longer keeps itself alive
two documented flags that do not exist
a kubeconfig fetch is not destructive, and never defaulted to ~/.kube/config
`doctor` as a name for the check that was already there
fix: run the suite on a non-UTF-8 machine, and stop one skill answering for another
Second-round fixes from the 2026-08-30 VCF 9.1 re-test; vmware-policy floor raised to 1.11.0 (the engine no longer fails open when rules.yaml cannot be read).

Kubeconfig session tokens no longer stored in the audit database. Parameter descriptions now reach the MCP JSON schema (0% -> 100% coverage); additionalProperties closed; vmware-policy floor raised to 1.10.0.
Six independent copies of the config-path rule reduced to one; the CLI now honours VMWARE_VKS_CONFIG; server.json starts the MCP server; Dockerfile can build.
A Workload Management failure was labelled a connectivity failure, because one try wrapped three checks. Failures are now attributed to the stage that raised them.
Fixes the server's self-reported version and the advertised tool count; adds a Claude Code plugin manifest.
Supervisor VM Service reads — VM snapshot / multi-NIC / VM groups via vm-operator CRDs (20→23), runtime-discovered version. Container Service not built (no CRD).
Moved to vmware-skills GitHub org; MCP Registry namespace → io.github.vmware-skills. Links updated.
CLI writes now route through the shared guard()+audit_call() core via @guarded, exactly like the MCP tools (HLD I-1/I-8). Requires vmware-policy>=1.8.8.
Remove read-only switch and approval tiers; read/write authz delegated to RBAC. Plus accumulated fixes since 1.8.5.
A failure that is returned is now audited as a failure, and certificate/URL detail no longer reaches the agent. Both fixes v1.8.4 announced were incomplete.
Teaching error messages, domain exceptions no longer redacted on the way to the agent, and tool descriptions that state when to use each tool and what to call next.
Per-target username can now come from an env var, resolved per access like the password; documented credential variables corrected against what each repo's code actually reads
MCP server moved into the package namespace — fixes two skills in one environment silently overwriting each other's server; agent-guardrails.md for local/small models now ships in every skill
Read-only mode now documented on every surface that teaches it (SKILL.md, setup-guide, capabilities) and reported by doctor
Read-only mode (9 tools withheld — both kubeconfig tools force-classified as writes), list-result envelope, declared environments
Session-probe eviction fix (dead cached sessions were never evicted; None currentSession now treated as dead) + lockfile mcp 1.28.1 clearing three GHSA HIGH advisories.
family version alignment (no code change)
Family version alignment to 1.7.4 (substantive change this cycle is in vmware-monitor: host-check boundary read batching).
Family version alignment (v1.7.3)
Graceful harbor listing + paginated TKC/workload lists
Family version alignment with v1.7.1 (AIops/Monitor large-inventory scale fix, issue #31).
guided init wizard + multi-path auth teaching
v1.6.1 .env password b64 obfuscation
v1.6.0 trust architecture: undo tokens + governance harness (budget/audit/risk-tiers)
v1.5.39: AIops snapshot-delete async + honest timeout (token-burn fix), Storage browse timeout fix; others version-aligned
backlog finish: one-command Supervisor auth preflight
backlog: fewer Supervisor round-trips
correct Supervisor authentication + safety fixes
Security hardening: safe error handling, TLS/path/permission fixes
